title: Harmonized brain ontology and 3D atlases for human, macaque, and marmoset basal ganglia
title_zh: 人类、猕猴和鼩猴基底节的调和脑本体学与3D图谱
abstract: A major goal of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is to create a suite of foundational reference cell atlases and associated standards for human and nonhuman primate brains. Central to this goal is the creation of cross-species-harmonized cellular taxonomies and structural parcellations with formal ontologies that can be mapped onto 3D reference frameworks, bridging neuroimaging and cellular and histological resolutions. We describe an iterative approach, focused initially on the basal ganglia, to co-create structural and cellular ontologies for human, macaque, and marmoset brains and to map and refine structural parcellations into neuroimaging-based common coordinate frameworks. We create a Harmonized Ontology of Mammalian Brain Anatomy (HOMBA) to meet these needs. These references provide the framework for documenting and mapping all experimental sampling in BICAN, allowing analyses of cellular and molecular variation as a function of topographic position and enabling comparisons of cellular, molecular, and neuroimaging-based functional variation across species.
abstract_zh: BRAIN细胞图谱网络（BICAN）的一个主要目标是为人类和非人灵长类大脑创建一套基础参考细胞图谱及相关标准。实现这一目标的关键在于建立跨物种调和的细胞分类学和结构分区，并制定可映射到3D参考框架的形式本体学，以连接神经影像学、细胞水平和组织学分辨率。我们描述了一种迭代方法，最初聚焦于基底节，以合作制定人类、猕猴和鼩猴大脑的结构与细胞本体学，并将结构分区映射和细化为基于神经影像学的通用坐标框架。我们创建了哺乳动物大脑解剖学调和本体学（HOMBA）以满足这些需求。这些参考资料为记录和映射BICAN中的所有实验采样提供了框架，使细胞与分子变异作为地形位置的函数进行分析成为可能，并能够跨物种比较细胞、分子和基于神经影像学的功能变异。
